title: What ISO 20022 migration taught us about data governance
linkedinPost:
44% of banks will miss the November 2026 SWIFT structured address deadline.

Not because they didn't migrate to ISO 20022.

Because they treated a data governance programme as a format upgrade — and left the underlying data untouched.

Finextra's Luuk De Vries put it precisely:

The gateway translation layer looked compliant. The source systems collecting payment instructions still used freetext. Structured-looking fields. Unstructured content inside them. No field ownership. No utilisation audit.

What I would actually do right now:

• Run a field utilisation audit — not a message compliance check. What % of optional fields carry real structured data vs empty or freetext values?
• Assign field ownership by business domain before November 2026. Remittance: finance. Address: operations. LEI: compliance.
• Identify one downstream AI or compliance use case — AML screening, DORA audit log, treasury reconciliation — and trace it to specific ISO 20022 fields. Build the business case from that dependency.
• Update upstream collection systems, not just the gateway. Enrichment at the gateway is a mask, not a fix.
• Wire structured fields directly into EU AI Act Article 12 logging. Every format conversion between collection and model input degrades your audit trail.

ISO 20022 structured data reduces AML false positive rates 20–40% (NICE Actimize, 2025). But only if the structured fields actually contain structured data. That is the governance question — not the migration one.

Revenue per employee in regulated financial services rises when payment data works harder. ISO 20022 is the infrastructure. Governance is what makes it real.

Full piece + the Data-First Migration Test I use to diagnose where firms are stuck — link in comments.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between ISO 20022 compliance and ISO 20022 data governance in banking?

acceptedAnswer.text: Compliance means your payment messages validate against the ISO 20022 schema — the format is correct. Data governance means the content inside those fields is accurate, structured, assigned to an identified business domain owner, and traceable into downstream systems. Compliance is a format check carried out at the gateway. Data governance is an organisational capability built across the full collection-to-settlement chain.

mainEntity.name: Why are so many banks still not ready for the November 2026 SWIFT structured address deadline?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because the November 2026 requirement — that structured postal address fields are populated in all CBPR+ cross-border messages — requires changes to upstream payment instruction collection systems, not just message translation layers. Banks that built migration capability around gateway translation discover their source systems still accept freetext. The deadline reveals the governance gap (Montran, 2026).

mainEntity.name: How does ISO 20022 data governance affect DORA compliance for financial services firms?

acceptedAnswer.text: DORA requires structured ICT incident logs. ISO 20022 fields — LEIs, value dates, instruction identifiers — are natural structured inputs to those logs. Firms with governed ISO 20022 data generate DORA-compliant audit trails programmatically. Firms without it reconstruct them manually, introducing latency, accuracy risk, and regulatory exposure during the incident response window.

mainEntity.name: How does ISO 20022 structured data improve AI model performance in financial services?

acceptedAnswer.text: AI models used in AML screening and fraud detection perform materially better on typed, validated inputs than on parsed freetext. ISO 20022 structured fields — party identifiers, structured remittance data, purpose codes — provide those typed inputs. NICE Actimize found this reduces false positive rates 20–40% compared to models operating on legacy MT freetext (NICE Actimize, 2025). The prerequisite is that the structured fields actually contain structured data — which requires governance, not just migration.
